title: Thirty coins.
paragraphs:
Thirty coins.
That’s all it took to sell perfection.

And somehow…
we’re still doing the same thing.

You may not be holding coins in your hands—
but you’ve traded Jesus before.

For approval.
For secret sin.
For one more moment of pleasure nobody sees.
Because this isn’t just Judas’ story.

You sing on Sunday…
but hide things Monday night.

You post Bible verses…
but entertain darkness in private.

You say “Lord, I love You”…
but your heart whispers, “Just this once…”

You’ve learned how to do it
without feeling anything anymore.

Not with betrayal—
but with small compromises.

A quiet justification.
A hidden click.
A “no one will know.”

Judas didn’t wake up one morning and say,
“I think I’ll betray Jesus today.”

Scripture says he handled the money…
and helped himself to it.
“He was a thief… he used to help himself to what was put into the money bag.” — John 12:6

Small theft.
Private sin.
Unseen corruption.
his heart grew cold enough to put a price on God.

“What are you willing to give me if I deliver Him over to you?”
So they counted out for him thirty pieces of silver. — Matthew 26:15

And heaven stood there in human flesh…
being valued like a slave.
“He shall give to their master thirty shekels of silver.” — Exodus 21:32
That was the worth of a servant.

And Judas looked at Jesus—
the Son of God—

How many times have you said
“This sin is worth it”
even for a moment?
But here’s where it breaks open.
Here’s where the story explodes into grace.

Because silver could only cover sin—
never remove it.
But the payment was never enough.
“For the life of a creature is in the blood… it is the blood that makes atonement for one’s life.” — Leviticus 17:11

They were all pointing forward—
whispering:
“You were not redeemed with perishable things like silver or gold… but with the precious blood of Christ, a lamb without blemish or defect.” — 1 Peter 1:18–19
But Jesus bought Judas’ kind of sinner with His life.

Even in betrayal…
Jesus was walking toward the cross.

Your hidden struggle.
Your double life.
Your silent guilt.

Some scholars interpret Judas’ story as a warning about hardened hearts—
a man who walked with Jesus but never truly surrendered.
Others see it as a tragic picture of remorse without repentance.
but he didn’t run to Jesus.
The other was crushed by shame.
This is where you decide your ending.

You’ve traded moments of God’s presence
for things that don’t last.
The same Jesus who was sold for silver…
Not when you “get your life together.”
Because the cross already paid it.
Jesus didn’t die for a better version of you.
He died for the real you.
You don’t just admire the cross.
You don’t just feel bad about sin.
“Repent, then, and turn to God, so that your sins may be wiped out…”
Drop the secret agreements with sin.
Grace is not permission to keep sinning.

Grace is Jesus stepping into your mess and saying,
“I already paid for this.”
Will you keep negotiating your soul?

“Jesus… I’ve traded You for lesser things.
Forgive me.
Wash me.
Take my life.”
He doesn’t bring up the price again.
Because He already paid it in full.
as a declaration that you’re done trading Jesus for temporary things.
